To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
HLA class I expression is increased on the surface of hepatocytes in patients with anti-HBe positive HBV infection and that this is not associated with activation of 2'-5' oligoadenylate synthetase.
the density of HLa class I protein on the hepatocytes was not increased in patients with HBeAg positive chronic hepatitis B infection.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the liver in the host immune response to hepatitis B virus ( HBV ) infection.
the study of the molecular basis of liver disease.
the role of the interferon system in chronic HBV infection and has shown that the interferon system is activated in the hepatocyte in chronic HBV infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the density of HBeAg positive HBV infected hepatocytes is not significantly increased above normal but levels of 5A synthetases are twice normal.

in HBeAg negative patients the density of class I HLA protein display is markedly increased in the absence of 2- 5A synthetases activity and in HBeAg-positive patients the density of the class I HLA is not increased in the presence or absence of 2 5 A synthetases activity.
the presence of anti-HBe in serum is a marker for type I interferon activity in the liver, while the presence of HBe antigen indicates the presence of type I interferon in the circulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in HBeAg-positive HBV infection, the liver is activated by type I IFN (alpha/beta) and in anti-HBe-positive HBV infection it is activated by type II IFN (gamma).

in HBeAg-positive patients, the liver has a high level of interferon activity and a low density of HLA-I protein display, while anti-HBe-positive patients have a low level of interferon and a high density of HLA protein.
HLA-I density is a good indicator of the type of interferon activity in HBV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the density of H2 class I proteins on the hepatocytes is not increased in HBeAg-positive chronic HBV infection, and that the activation of hepatic 2-5 A synthetase in these patients is probably mediated by alpha or beta interferon.
HLA class I density on hepatocytes of patients infected with hepatitis B is related to type of interferon activation.
the density of HLa class I protein on hepatocytes is not a good indicator of the degree of interferon activity in these cells.
